questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion to emphasise the idea that *‘the decision was taken without consulting the team’*?
options: Without consulting the team was the decision taken.
The decision was taken without consulting the team by them.
It was the team that the decision was taken without consulting.
Had they consulted, the decision would never have been taken.
questions.answer: Without consulting the team was the decision taken.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly employs a cleft construction to clarify *‘the reason the project failed was poor planning’*?
options: The failure of the project was due to poor planning.
It was poor planning that the project failed.
The reason the project failed was because of planning issues.
What caused the project to fail was a lack of foresight.
questions.answer: It was poor planning that the project failed.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive to express a hypothetical scenario where *‘the government should ban plastic bags’*?
options: If the government bans plastic bags, it will reduce pollution.
The government must ban plastic bags to solve the problem.
If they banned plastic bags, it would be the right decision.
Had the government banned plastic bags, we would have seen results immediately.
questions.answer: If they banned plastic bags, it would be the right decision.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly employs ellipsis in a complex sentence to avoid redundancy while maintaining formality?
options: She wanted to go, but she didn’t have enough time, so she stayed at home.
After finishing her work, she left the office, which was late.
He said he would help, but he never showed up, which was disappointing.
They agreed to meet at noon, but they didn’t arrive until later, which was unexpected.
questions.answer: They agreed to meet at noon, but they didn’t arrive until later, which was unexpected.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a nuanced choice of verb form to express *‘a situation where the speaker doubts the truth of an assertion despite knowing it was once true’*?
options: He claims he saw the ghost, but I doubt it.
He insists he saw the ghost, but I still believe it happened.
He swore he saw the ghost, but I can’t trust his word now.
He used to say he saw the ghost, but he’s lying now.
questions.answer: He swore he saw the ghost, but I can’t trust his word now.
